definitions.full: H5291. naarah II. נַעֲרָה noun feminine girl, damsel ; — absolute ׳נ Judg 19:3 22 t., also Qr Gen 24:14 20 t. Genesis, Deuteronomy ( נַעֲרָה Kt in Pentateuch only Deut 22:19 , see below); plural absolute נְעָרוֺת 1Sam 9:11 +, construct נַעֲרוֺת Est 4:4 ; suffix נַעֲרוֺתָיו Ruth 2:22 ; 3:2 , נַעֲרֹתֶיהָ Gen 24:61 ; Exod 2:5 , etc.; — 1 girl, damsel ; ׳נ קְטַנָּה little girl only 2Kin 5:2 , compare 5:4 , perhaps = young daughters Job 40:29; elsewhere = young woman 1Sam 9:11 ; especially as marriageable, Gen 24:14 , 16 , 28 , 55 , 57 ; 34:3 , 12 (all J), Deut 22:15 (twice in verse); 22:16 , 19 , 20 , 21 , 24 , 26 (twice in verse); 22:29 ; 1Kin 1:3-4 , Est 2:4 , 7 , 8 , 9 , 12 (twice in verse); 2:13 ; specifically virgin ׳נ בְּתוּלָה Judg 21:12 ; Deut 22:23 , 28 ; 1Kin 1:2 ; Est 2:2-3 ,(compare Deut 22:15 b; 22:20 ); ׳נ מְאֹרָשָׂה betrothed girl 22:25 , 27 ; young widow Ruth 2:6 ; 4:12 ; of a concubine Judg 19:3-4 , 5 , 6 , 8 , 9 , a prostitute Amos 2:7 . 2 of female attendants , maids (always plural), Gen 24:61 (J), Exod 2:5 (E), 1Sam 25:42 ; Prov 9:3 ; 27:27 ; 31:15 ; Est 2:9 (twice in verse); 4:4 , 16 ; gleaners Ruth 2:5 , 8 , 22 , 23 ; 3:2 . — Note. נער Kt in Pentateuch as feminine (Qr נַעֲרָ֯ ) is probably not original; it is not found in Sam. Pentateuch, and feminine plural נַעֲרֹתֶיהָ occurs Genesis, Exodus; compare Ges §§ 2n , 17c.
